data.narrative:
Gauss Fusion is a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Milena Roveda that has raised €9M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 11 total peers (3 public, 8 private) in the nuclear energy sector, including Fuse Energy, Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, and X-Energy.

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the €9M raised as a proxy base and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, implying a valuation of €18M. The peer-median method compares against three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies: Fuse Energy at $200M (Series A), Nano Nuclear Energy at $808M (Seed), and Valar Atomics at $6.0B (Series B). The median across these three peers yields $808M, with a range spanning $200M to $6.0B.

Triangulation of these methods produces a low bound of $15.3M, a median of $413M, and a high bound of $929M. The wide dispersion reflects stage and maturity divergence within the peer set—particularly the 30x gap between the Series A floor ($200M) and the Series B outlier ($6.0B). Key uncertainties include technology validation status, IP differentiation within fusion subsector, and capital intensity to next inflection. A valuation toward the lower-to-median range ($15M–$250M) would be more defensible absent evidence of advanced technical or commercial traction relative to Fuse Energy's comparable stage positioning.
